patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 4's first/second rotor-groove gas ports and corresponding slide-valve ports/interfaces are supported by the passages describing adjacent grooves opening respectively to first and second ports (b4aef000688830e9e72a04be17bdc39c; b65fd4e51433bafb4f6b5a7dd4f4118c). The two downstream passage ports and valve-to-casing mating are supported by the first/second passage correspondence in 1bd5120252f0fb6ffd6ce5fece75fc53 and gas paths in b65fd4e51433bafb4f6b5a7dd4f4118c. The model does not include claim 2's second partition wall; its warning appropriately notes the omission. No unsupported pressure, drive, or controller facts are asserted.

functional_completeness.rationale: The flat component set includes screw rotor, gate rotor, casing, and slide valve; behavior describes chamber formation/compression, partitioned discharge to the paired ports, and downstream passage flow. This covers the selected claim-1 compressor scope. The model appropriately omits unsupported external drive/source/sink components.

flow_consistency.rationale: Revision 4 resolves the prior gaps: first and second groove gas outputs mate to the corresponding valve port inputs, and the two valve passage outputs mate separately to respective casing passage inputs. All connected port flow_types are gas and directions are compatible (out-to-in); flow references preserve the paired paths.

claim_traceability.rationale: Both requirements identify claim 1 in their rationale and map to relevant subsystems. The second-partition-wall feature of claim 2 is not represented as a requirement or component; the warning distinguishes that optional scope.

interfaces.rationale: Each interface references existing subsystem IDs, valid local/mate port IDs, and an existing flow reference. The paired chamber/groove-to-slide-valve and valve-to-casing boundaries are each represented once, using distinct paths and compatible gas ports.

textbook_application.rationale: The model uses physical patent-named components, separates behavior from physical structure, and records interfaces/flows without inventing controller or detailed state behavior. This is consistent with modeling guidance; textbook evidence is not used to support invention facts.

summary: Revision 4 resolves the prior casing-port mating and missing groove-to-slide-valve connectivity issues. Patent passages support the paired groove/port correspondence and the respective downstream discharge passages. Full SJS review found no remaining actionable grounding, completeness, flow, traceability, interface, or textbook-application issues. All six checklist categories pass; no unresolved findings.
